StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldFlush.issue: The predicate itself is faithful -- false for the owner, true otherwise (RetainHandPower.cs:19-26), and the sim's should_flush_hand has no player parameter at all, which is a single-player tautology. What differs is what a FALSE result means, and that is turn_structure's G4, which is already LIVE and is not re-verdicted here per binding rule 3: C#'s FlushPlayerHand treats false as 'every card is retained' and then still runs Hook.AfterFlush and PlayerCombatState.EndOfTurnCleanup unconditionally (CombatManager.cs:1327-1346), where combat.py:661-662 guards the whole thing (`if should_flush_hand(): discard_hand()`) so a false result skips on_hand_emptied as well -- and there is no after_flush hook in hooks.py to fire in the first place. Recorded from this end because this power is the sim's ONLY should_flush_hand implementer, i.e. G4's entire trigger surface in the power tier.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: A DELIBERATE SLOT SHIFT that is observationally correct in the normal case and LIVE through turn_structure's G3 in the extra-turn case. C# decrements at the PLAYER side's Hook.AfterTurnEnd (CombatManager.cs:1307), i.e. after FlushPlayerHand (:1296); the sim ticks at on_enemy_side_end (combat.py:345) instead, and its docstring (powers.py:3531-3533) explains the choice as 'the sim's equivalent post-flush slot'. That reasoning is unnecessary -- after_player_turn_end (combat.py:665) IS the sim's post-flush player-side slot and is unused -- but harmless in the normal case, because on_enemy_side_end still falls between the player's turn N end and turn N+1 start, so Retain Hand 1 retains exactly one hand on both sides. EXECUTED, and it does NOT survive an extra turn: with a should_take_extra_turn listener registered (the shape of the ported Ancient relic Pael's Eye, relics/paels_eye.py:36-46), one end_turn leaves `Retain Hand(1)` still on the player, where the same end_turn without it leaves None. combat.py:648-652 short-circuits at the TOP of end_turn and never reaches on_player_turn_end, the flush, after_player_turn_end OR the enemy turn, so the tick never happens; C# evaluates ShouldTakeExtraTurn in SwitchFromPlayerToEnemySide (CombatManager.cs:1360-1373) AFTER both EndPlayerTurnPhase methods, so Hook.AfterTurnEnd at :1307 has already decremented. The root cause is turn_structure's G3, already LIVE and not re-verdicted; this is a concrete content instance of it, and note that moving the tick to after_player_turn_end would NOT fix it, because combat.py:648-652 skips that too.

guards.rationale: The sim's on_enemy_side_end takes no argument and the power does not filter (powers.py:3542-3543) -- it does not need to, since the slot is reached once per round and this power is player-only in ported content (Equilibrium / Salvo). Note that the shifted slot means the filter C# needs is exactly the filter the sim cannot express there.

The sim's Power._tick (powers.py:70-75) decrements the field and _expires at <= 0 where C# routes through PowerCmd.Decrement -> ModifyAmount -> ShouldRemoveDueToAmount (PowerCmd.cs:215-250) -- Decrement, not TickDownDuration, so neither side honours SkipNextDurationTick. Observationally identical for a Buff: ModifyAmount's only unconditional modifier leg is Hook.ModifyPowerAmountReceived (PowerCmd.cs:234), whose ported listeners are ArtifactPower (Debuff-only) and RuinedHelmet (StrengthPower-only). Same mechanism and same verdict as audit/records/power/colossus.json's AfterSideTurnEnd guard, per binding rule 3.

guards.what: Interaction with the per-card Retain keyword
guards.rationale: The sim's discard_hand keeps cards with card.retain (player.py:192-196) independently of this power, which is C#'s per-card ShouldRetainThisTurn path. Two independent mechanisms on both sides; this power's false ShouldFlush short-circuits the whole flush, so the per-card path is moot when it is active.
